Order service API

All responses are JSON unless noted. Requests are made to the address this service is running on.

GET /docs
    This page (plain text).

GET /value
    Returns {"value": <integer>}. No authentication.

POST /token
    Returns {"token": "<token>"}. No authentication. Send the token on authenticated
    requests in the header "Authorization: Bearer <token>".

GET /orders?page=N
    Authenticated. Lists orders, 50 per page; N starts at 1.
    Returns {"page", "total_pages", "items", "next"}. "next" is the path of the following
    page, or null on the last page.
    Each order has: id, customer_id, status, placed_at, amount_cents.
    status is one of: placed, shipped, cancelled, returned.
    placed_at is an ISO 8601 timestamp. amount_cents is an integer number of cents.

GET /customers/{id}
    Authenticated. Returns {"id", "name", "region", "tier", "discount_pct"}; 404 if the id is unknown.
    region is one of: north, south, east, west. discount_pct is a whole-number percentage.

content.text:
I've written `result.json` in the workspace root. Shipped orders placed 1 March to 31 May 2025 (UTC) come to **9,329,707 cents** across **407** distinct orders.

| Region | Cents |
|---|---|
| north | 2,666,579 |
| south | 2,714,624 |
| east | 1,671,579 |
| west | 2,276,925 |

`duplicates_skipped` is 20. The 1,500 listings were 1,480 distinct orders, and every repeated listing was identical to the first one I saw. These are not all in the qualifying set, because I counted repeats of any order.

- **Checks:** the by-region values add up to `total_cents`, and the file has exactly the four requested keys. Each order is counted once. The date range is applied on the UTC instant, from 1 March 00:00 UTC up to but not including 1 June 00:00 UTC. The status filter is an exact match on "shipped". Each order is discounted and rounded half up to a whole cent individually.
- **Coverage:** I fetched all 30 pages, and every customer id on a qualifying order resolved, so none were missing.
- **Retries:** the service was flaky as warned. Over the whole run it returned 13 rate-limit responses and 12 expired-token responses. I waited the stated time, or fetched a new token, and repeated each request. Nothing was skipped or guessed.
- **What surprised me:** nothing beyond the above. The duplicates, mixed UTC offsets and short-lived tokens were all expected. Timestamps used six different offsets, and none were missing an offset.

I kept the working script in `/tmp/work`, outside the workspace.
